questions.prompt: What main claim does Chapter 7 make about willpower?
choices: Willpower is equally available at every hour
Willpower is not permanently on-call with the same strength
Willpower only matters in school settings

explanation.gentle: The chapter says serious effort is not equally available at every moment.
explanation.direct: Keller rejects the fantasy of endlessly on-demand willpower.
explanation.competitive: Not every hour can carry the same force.

questions.prompt: Why does timing matter in Chapter 7?
choices: Because all late-day work is worthless
Because hard work is weakened when it is placed after strength is already spent
Because mood should control every decision

explanation.gentle: The chapter says bad timing creates an avoidable tax on meaningful work.
explanation.direct: Placement affects the quality of force the task receives.
explanation.competitive: Weak windows make the hard thing pay extra.

questions.prompt: What is the chapter actually criticizing?
choices: Scheduling hard work as if all hours are equal
Having any routine at all
Doing small tasks before lunch

explanation.gentle: The chapter attacks the assumption that serious effort can be summoned with equal strength whenever convenient.
explanation.direct: Uniform scheduling is the lie under attack.
explanation.competitive: Treating every slot as equal is how depth gets weakened.

questions.prompt: Aria has one fresh early block before reactive meetings and messages arrive. What best fits Chapter 7?
choices: Spend the fresh block on small requests and rescue the memo later
Use the fresh block for the hardest memo
Wait until the afternoon pressure makes the memo feel urgent

explanation.gentle: The hardest task should meet the strongest realistic window.
explanation.direct: Protect the fresh block for the work needing judgment.
explanation.competitive: Give the memo the clean hour before noise steals it.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would Chapter 7 reject as false?
choices: Important work should respect strong and weak windows
If a task matters, discipline should rescue it equally well at any hour
Bad timing can weaken serious effort before it begins

explanation.gentle: The chapter rejects the heroic fantasy that all hours can carry the same serious effort.
explanation.direct: Not every slot is equal territory for meaningful work.
explanation.competitive: The rescue myth is exactly what Keller breaks.

questions.prompt: Damon keeps pushing his hardest reading to late night after a draining day. What did Chapter 7 say he missed?
choices: The value of more colorful notes
The need to study only in groups
The danger of placing the hard task in a depleted slot

explanation.gentle: The issue was not only effort. The hard material never got the fresher window.
explanation.direct: He kept feeding the demanding task a weak hour.
explanation.competitive: The text kept getting scraps and then blamed his character.

questions.prompt: What limit keeps Chapter 7 from turning into excuse-making?
choices: Timing should sharpen action, not justify endless delay
The chapter only applies to work tasks
Weak energy automatically excuses all hard effort

explanation.gentle: The chapter says respect timing, but do not hide behind it forever.
explanation.direct: Wise placement is not permission for permanent postponement.
explanation.competitive: Use the window. Do not worship it.

questions.prompt: Leila wants to move an important family decision out of an exhausted evening and into a clearer window. What is the best Chapter 7 response?
choices: That is weak because important conversations should happen immediately no matter what
That only matters for workplace decisions
That is wise placement if it protects clarity rather than avoiding the issue

explanation.gentle: The chapter says better timing can be a form of responsibility, not just delay.
explanation.direct: Match meaningful judgment to the clearer state.
explanation.competitive: Refusing a bad hour can be stronger than forcing a weak conversation through it.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 7 build on Chapter 6?
choices: It explains that the right routine still needs the right timing window
It says discipline no longer matters once timing is understood
It abandons support routines in favor of spontaneity

explanation.gentle: Chapter 6 chooses the hinge routine, and Chapter 7 says the routine still has to meet a strong window.
explanation.direct: Structure without good placement stays weaker than it should.
explanation.competitive: The hinge routine matters, but the hour still matters too.

questions.prompt: Which action best applies Chapter 7 to a reactive day?
choices: Spend the strongest hour on maintenance work and trust late heroics to cover the rest
Treat every hour as equal and focus only on attitude
Protect the strongest realistic window for the task needing the most depth

explanation.gentle: The chapter works when the strong window is reserved for the task carrying the most consequence.
explanation.direct: Protect the best force for the work that most needs it.
explanation.competitive: Do not waste prime force on noise and then beg discipline to rescue the hard thing later.
